mission: Key API request limits and admin login counters by the platform client-IP header, through one shared helper. The value must be a single valid IP address; IPv6 is grouped by /64. Outside development a missing or invalid value shares one strict key. Admin login keeps three counters: email plus client and client across emails (unchanged numbers), and an account ceiling of 20 failed attempts per hour, then a 30 minute lock. A successful login clears the email counters only. No reset tool. Client keys in rate-limit log lines are hashed. The existing admin rate-limit status page adds integer request-key counts since process start, with no addresses. Owner approval is under security_or_secrets_policy only.

impacts.reason: New shared helper: the client key from the platform client-IP header, validated as one IP address, IPv6 grouped by /64, a strict shared key outside development when missing or invalid, and the connection address in development only.

The request limiter keys by the shared helper, hashes client keys in its log lines, logs the shared key at most once per window, and keeps lock-guarded per-process request-key counts for the status page. Collector keys for /me are unchanged.

Three counters: email plus client and client across emails at the existing settings, and an account ceiling of 20 per 3600 s with an 1800 s lock. Success clears the email counters, never the client counter. Earlier account keys are left to expire.
The admin login uses the shared helper for its client key, so every counter always applies.
The rate-limit status response adds started_at and three integer counts. Existing fields are unchanged.
Covers other forwarding headers, missing and invalid values, IPv6 /64 grouping, development fallback and parsed-address comparison.
Covers shared buckets, the strict shared key, hashed log keys, each status count, counts while disabled, no addresses in the status body, and 401 without or with a wrong admin token.
Router tests for the email plus client lock, the account ceiling across clients, and the client counter on the strict shared key.
Unit tests for the three counters, the account ceiling numbers, what a successful login clears, and a required client key.
Status page counts, keying behind a proxy, and what to do when admin login is temporarily unavailable.
Rate limiting is keyed by the platform client-IP header with a strict shared key.

resources: Staging Redis admin login counters (new key shapes, existing keys expire)
impact.deployment_impact: The API rebuilds through its GitHub watch because the API service changed. No collector runtime input change, no schema change, no website change. see private review

recovery.procedure: Native revert PR of this merge with its own docs/agent/missions/<name>.json. New Redis keys expire on their own.
recovery.backup: Not applicable: no schema or row change.
